explanations: luna: The section's root ه د ي describes showing the way; the opening prayer asks God to guide its speaker onto the straight path, making guidance a request from the traveler. | terra: “Guide us to the straight path” is the direct prayer to be shown and led along the right road.
luna: The section's guided route is distinguished from the wretched road; this ayah names the path of those favored and contrasts it with those who incur anger or stray.
terra: At the descent from the garden, following God’s guidance secures the travellers from fear and grief, paralleling the later Adamic promise in 20:123.

luna: The section's dictionary form سَوَاءٌ names an even middle; this ayah says one who exchanges faith for disbelief has lost the سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ, joining the middle-place sense to a lost road. | terra: Whoever exchanges faith for unbelief “has strayed from the middle of the road,” directly joining سوء choice to سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ.

luna: The section names root ي س ر for ease and contrasts it with difficulty; this ayah says God wants ease for people and does not want hardship, in a concrete rule about fasting. | terra: يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْر states the divine preference for ease over hardship in the same paired vocabulary.
terra: فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ combines what is readily available from يسر with الهدي as sacrificial livestock, making the two root families meet in an actual led animal.
terra: Rejecting false power and holding the firm handhold combines right avoidance with secure support, reversing both the object avoided and the unsupported traveller.
terra: A debtor in hardship is granted delay until مَيْسَرَةٍ, presenting ease as a reachable condition that answers present constriction.
terra: If a debtor is weak or unable to dictate, his guardian speaks justly for him; it is a precise legal scene of a weak person proceeding through another’s support.
terra: Pilgrimage is owed by whoever can find a way to the House; ability and access determine whether the sacred journey is practicable.
luna: The section distinguishes a guided road from turning aside; this ayah accuses people of trying to make God's way crooked and seeking to lead believers from it.

luna: The section's root ه د ي also has a dictionary sense of a weak, swaying walker supported by two people; this ayah says human beings are weak and God wants to lighten their burden, a thematic echo rather than a walking scene. | terra: God wants to lighten the human being because humanity was created weak; lightness answers precisely to the section’s weak supported walker and light legs.
luna: The section's guide points a traveler along a way; this ayah describes people who want others to lose the path, making deliberate misdirection the opposing act.
terra: The oppressed men, women, and children ask for a protecting ally and helper; this parallels dependence on companions, though no walking scene is present.
terra: The truly helpless are those without a means and unable to find a way, joining human weakness to the practical inability to be guided onto a route.
terra: After covenant obligations and a promise of support, disbelief is said to stray from سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ, the road’s balanced middle.
terra: Through revelation God guides seekers of His pleasure along paths of peace and onto a straight path, making the scripture an active route guide.
terra: People who follow earlier desires are said to have gone astray from سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ, making the middle road something inherited error can leave.
terra: Believers are commanded فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ concerning intoxicants, gambling, cult stones, and divining arrows; avoidance receives the right harmful object rather than the reminder.
terra: Satan uses intoxicants and gambling to bar people from God’s remembrance and prayer, explaining why the preceding ayah commands avoiding them instead of being diverted from reminder.
terra: هَدْيًا بَالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ uses هدي for an offering that reaches the Kaaba, a different root sense whose animal is assigned a destination.
terra: The stars are made so people may find guidance through darkness on land and sea, identifying created signs that go before the traveller.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance and pairs ease with difficulty; this ayah describes guidance as an opened heart and misguidance as constriction like climbing into the sky, joining direction to felt ease or strain. | terra: Guidance opens the chest, while misguidance makes it tight “as though climbing into the sky”; moral direction is felt as easy passage versus punishing ascent.

luna: The section develops a route and the remembrance that distinguishes its traveler; this ayah names the Lord's straight path and says its signs are made clear for people who remember, continuing 6:125's guidance contrast.
terra: The same ayah names livestock made for carrying loads and forbids following Satan’s footsteps, bringing the pack animal and the choice of whom to follow together.
terra: الْحَوَايَا means entrails here, not a saddle cloth, yet its enclosing root occurs beside what animals’ backs bear and so illuminates the haviyye word-family cautiously.

luna: The section says the road may be one while the traveler's response differs; this ayah commands following one straight path and warns against side paths that divide people from it. | terra: God’s straight path is to be followed, while following the other roads disperses travellers away from it; the journey forks by obedience.
terra: The Prophet declares that his Lord guided him to a straight path, the upright religion of Abraham, joining prophetic route and the named patriarch.
luna: The section's guide goes ahead to show a route; this ayah reverses the role by putting Satan in wait on God's straight path to intercept its travelers.
luna: The section says the same road's travelers differ in how they proceed; this ayah continues Satan's threat to approach people from every direction, showing how the straight path is resisted.
terra: Wrongdoers sit on every path threatening people and barring believers from God’s way, turning the roadside itself into an obstacle to guidance.
terra: The arrogant see the path of right guidance and refuse it, but see the path of error and take it, making the wrong route a deliberate preference.
terra: The command “follow him so that you may be guided” makes following the Messenger the human motion corresponding to divine guidance.
terra: God lightens the believers’ duty because He knows weakness is among them, again pairing ضعف with divinely granted lightness.
terra: A near gain and moderate journey would have drawn followers, but the actual distance seemed hard; ease and hardship expose the quality of following.
terra: Those who ask the Prophet for mounts but find nothing to carry them turn away in tears, making lack of a vehicle the concrete limit on willing followers.
terra: God does not let a people stray after guiding them until He clarifies what they must guard against, holding guidance and right avoidance in one rule.
terra: Travellers enjoy a ship’s good wind and then face a storm, staging ease and distress as two experiences on the same vehicle and route.
terra: God calls to the abode of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path, joining invitation, road, and destination.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for a guide who goes ahead; this ayah asks whether the one who guides to truth is more worthy to follow than one who cannot find the way without being guided. | terra: The ayah asks whether the one who guides to truth deserves to be followed over one who cannot proceed unless guided, exposing leader and dependent follower.
terra: Noah commands his people to board the ark in God’s name, marking the beginning and course of the vehicle journey that ends when it settles in 11:44.
terra: The ark “settled on al-Judi” in وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ, extending the rider’s settling sense from an animal to a vessel after travel.
terra: Pharaoh goes ahead of his people on the Day of Judgment and brings them to the Fire, the exact inverse of a guide preceding followers toward safety.

luna: The section names root ش ق و for hardship and the wretched; this ayah divides people at the final hour into wretched and blessed, framing the outcomes named in 11:106 and 108. | terra: The Day divides people into شَقِيّ and سَعِيد; the next ayah supplies the wretched group’s fiery destination.

luna: The section names root ش ق و for the wretched traveler who reaches the Fire; this ayah places the wretched in Hell, where they groan and cry out. | terra: Those who are شَقُوا are in the Fire, another direct bond between wretchedness and the fiery endpoint.

luna: The section's wrong road ends in fire; this adjacent ayah gives the opposite end to the blessed, who remain in the Garden. | terra: Those made happy are in the Garden with an unbroken gift, the destination opposite the fire of the شَقُوا in 11:106.
terra: The Prophet calls “this is my way” and names himself and those who follow him, giving the mission a leader-and-followers road form.
terra: God subjects ships to run through the sea by His command, giving the vehicle the compliant following that the section assigns to the easy-guided mount.

luna: The section names root ج ن ب for keeping something away and shows the wretched person keeping the reminder aside; Abraham instead asks God to keep him and his sons away from idol worship. | terra: Abraham asks وَاجْنُبْنِي وَبَنِيَّ to be kept away from idols; the same root works rightly by removing the worshipper from the false object.
luna: The section cites Abraham's request to be kept away from idols; this neighboring ayah says idols led many astray and distinguishes those who follow Abraham, explaining his request.
terra: Livestock provide beauty when driven home and sent out, a controlled herd movement related to the animal led calmly beside its keeper.

luna: The section pictures an easy mount carrying its rider along a route; this ayah says livestock carry loads to distant lands people could not reach without hardship, making the mount's easing function concrete. | terra: Livestock carry burdens to a land people could reach only بِشِقِّ الْأَنْفُسِ; the mount converts bodily hardship into attainable travel.

luna: The section adds a mount to the promise of ease; this ayah names horses, mules, and donkeys as animals for riding, supplying the literal mount scene. | terra: Horses, mules, and donkeys are created لِتَرْكَبُوهَا, supplying the literal riding animals beneath the section’s easy-guided mount.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for showing the route; this ayah says God directs the way while some routes are crooked, making guidance and deviation two actual directions. | terra: God owns the path’s intended direction, while “some of it deviates”; guidance and the road’s lateral departure are held in one image.

luna: The section develops a mountain ascent and a road that can be guided; this ayah places paths among mountains and rivers so people may find their way. | terra: Mountains stabilize the earth and rivers and roads are provided “so that you may be guided,” placing guidance in a traversable landscape.
terra: Landmarks and stars supply the traveller’s means of guidance, completing the preceding ayah’s roads.
terra: Every messenger commands worship of God and avoidance of false powers; the ayah then distinguishes those guided from those fixed in error.
terra: The bee is told to eat from fruits and travel its Lord’s paths ذُلُلًا, joining an animal, divinely given routes, and docile ease in one formulation.
terra: A dependent man is a burden wherever his master directs him, while the other commands justice “and is on a straight path”; ability and manner divide travellers.

luna: The section's dictionary form السَّوِيَّة is a covering placed over a camel's hump; this ayah depicts portable animal-hide dwellings used in travel and at rest, a related but different use of animal covering.
terra: A foot can slip after being firm because one barred others from God’s path; wrong allegiance becomes loss of footing on the road.
terra: God chooses Abraham and guides him to a straight path, making the figure named at surah 87’s close a traveller under divine guidance.
terra: The Qur’an guides to “that which is most upright,” making the reminder itself the guide walking ahead on the best-aligned course.

luna: The section's wider surah contrasts preferring worldly life with the lasting Hereafter; this ayah describes the one who wants the immediate life and assigns Hell as his outcome, setting up 17:19's opposite course.
luna: The section contrasts the nearer life with the better, lasting Hereafter; this ayah describes the believer who seeks the Hereafter and strives for it, the other course to 17:18.
terra: The ban on strutting adds that the walker can neither split the earth nor reach the mountains in height, opposing calm gait while joining walking to ascent.
terra: Human beings are carried on land and sea, a broad vehicle image that supports the section’s traveller without specifying a mount’s docility.
terra: The same phrase أَعْرَضَ وَنَأَى بِجَانِبِهِ pictures the recipient of favor turning away to his side, rather than continuing behind the guide.
terra: Each person acts according to his own manner, while God knows who is “more guided in way”; this closely states that the road differs through its walker.
terra: The ayah contrasts God’s guidance with loss of guides, then gathers the lost on their faces toward Hell, turning misguidance into a bodily procession.
terra: The cave youths ask God to “prepare for us from our affair right conduct”; preparing a fit course parallels the dictionary sense of ease as readiness.
terra: God will “prepare for you facility in your affair,” a nonlexical parallel to being made ready for the easier course.
terra: The sun veers to the cave’s right and passes its left while the ayah closes with God’s guidance, bringing lateral avoidance and true guidance into one scene.

luna: The section says the wretched person turns aside from the reminder; this ayah describes someone who is reminded of God's signs and turns away, then says he will not be guided when called to guidance. | terra: One who is reminded of God’s signs and turns away is veiled from understanding and will not be guided, joining avoided reminder to blocked guidance.
terra: Moses and his servant return, retracing their own footprints after recognizing the missed sign, a literal correction of direction on a learning journey.
terra: Moses asks to follow the knowledgeable servant so that he may teach him right guidance, staging learner behind guide on a shared journey.
terra: فَسَنَقُولُ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا is another future promise of ease in a person’s appointed affair, close in stance to 87:8.
terra: Zechariah says he has never been شَقِيًّا in calling upon his Lord, a prayerful negation of the root without an explicit road scene.
terra: Jesus says God did not make him overbearing and شَقِيًّا, a character-level negation of the wretched figure who turns aside from reminder.
terra: Abraham says “follow me; I will guide you to an even path,” explicitly staging a guide in front, a follower, and صِرَاطًا سَوِيًّا.
terra: Abraham withdraws from the idols his people invoke and hopes not to be شَقِيًّا in prayer, joining right separation from idols to escape from wretchedness.
terra: The God-fearing are gathered to the Merciful as an honored delegation, giving their final journey a dignified manner of arrival.
terra: The criminals are driven thirsty to Hell, opposing the preceding delegation in both manner and destination.

luna: The section names root ي س ر for making the Prophet's task easy and pairs it with reminding; this ayah says the Qur'an was made easy on Muhammad's tongue to warn and give good news. | terra: The Qur’an is made easy on the Prophet’s tongue so he may give good news and warn, joining prophetic readiness to effective reminder.

luna: The section names root ش ق و for hardship; God tells Muhammad that the Qur'an was not sent down to make him wretched, a direct boundary on the section's promise of ease. | terra: The Qur’an was not sent to the Prophet لِتَشْقَى, so revelation and his commission are expressly bounded away from the section’s hardship root.
luna: The section pairs ease for the Prophet with a reminder for the one who fears; this neighboring ayah says the Qur'an is a reminder for the God-fearing, specifying the purpose after 20:2.

luna: The section names root ي س ر for ease; Moses asks God to make his task easy, a second prophetic request that places ease inside an undertaking. | terra: Moses asks وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي, the same root as the promise to make the Prophet fit for the easiest course.
terra: Moses asks for a minister from his family, initiating the companion-support scene that becomes explicit in 20:31.
terra: Naming Aaron as the requested minister identifies the person on whom Moses’ back and mission will rely.
terra: Moses asks God to strengthen his back through Aaron, a concrete human counterpart to the weak person who moves by leaning on companions.
terra: Moses asks that Aaron share his task, turning support into companionship along the commissioned journey.

luna: The section's root ه د ي describes leading along a way; Moses answers that the Lord gives each thing its form and then guides it, bringing the section's creation-and-guidance sequence into one formulation. | terra: “He gave each thing its created form, then guided” restages 87:2-3 as a single answer: fitting a creature and directing it belong together.

luna: The section treats the route as a way God makes accessible; this ayah says God made paths through the earth for people, connecting creation with passage. | terra: God spreads the earth as a cradle and threads roads through it for people, the physical counterpart to His giving each creature form and guidance in 20:50.
terra: مَكَانًا سُوًى names an equally accessible middle meeting place, exactly the spatial sense cited in the section.
luna: The section's full surah ends its wrong road in a Fire where one neither dies nor lives; this ayah gives that same boundary to the criminal who comes to his Lord.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance and develops a route made easy; this ayah tells Moses to make a dry path through the sea and promises the travelers will not fear pursuit. | terra: Moses is commanded to take God’s servants by night and strike a dry road through the sea, a guide leading followers on a divinely prepared path without fear.

luna: The section says the course taken determines its outcome; this ayah shows Pharaoh and his troops pursuing the sea path and being overwhelmed, completing 20:77's safe crossing with the pursuers' fate. | terra: Pharaoh follows the guided party with his forces and is overwhelmed by the sea, showing the disastrous pursuer on the same opened route.

luna: The section's root ه د ي names the guide who leads forward; this ayah says Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them, explaining the failed pursuit in 20:78. | terra: The passage concludes that Pharaoh misled his people and did not guide them, explicitly judging the false leader’s direction.

luna: The section names root ش ق و for hardship; God warns Adam that expulsion from the garden would leave him struggling, giving misery a concrete life-and-provision setting. | terra: Adam is warned that leaving the garden will make him تَشْقَى, locating hardship at the far end of a wrong departure.

luna: The section names root ش ق و for hardship; this ayah promises that whoever follows God's guidance will neither stray nor become wretched, directly linking the right route to release from misery. | terra: Whoever follows God’s guidance “will neither stray nor suffer”; following the leader prevents both loss of route and the شقاء opposed to ease.

luna: The section's worst traveler keeps the reminder aside; this ayah gives that turning away its own consequence, a constricted life and gathering blind, completing 20:123's promise about following guidance. | terra: Turning away from God’s reminder produces a constricted life immediately after the promise that following guidance prevents straying and wretchedness.
terra: صِرَاطِ السَّوِيِّ and وَمَنِ اهْتَدَى bring the section’s “middle/even place” and guidance roots together in one question about whose route proves right.

luna: The section places a hard ascent on the route; this ayah describes mountains and broad paths laid through them, a physical setting for guided passage. | terra: Firm mountains contain broad passes “so that they may be guided,” making guidance movement through mountain openings.
terra: Abraham’s line are made leaders who guide by God’s command, stating the forward human leadership implicit in the section’s definition of هادي.
terra: The disputant twists his side in order to mislead others from God’s path, joining bodily side-turning to active diversion from the road.

luna: The section follows a road journey with a mount; this ayah depicts pilgrims arriving on foot and on lean camels from distant passes. | terra: Pilgrims arrive on foot and “on every lean camel” from every deep mountain road, joining gait, mount, and long pass.
terra: The command to avoid the pollution of idols gives the same avoidance action the right object, unlike keeping divine reminder at one’s side.
terra: The sacrificial camels fall عَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهَا, onto their sides; this animal scene preserves the concrete “side” beneath the section’s جنب word-family.
terra: Those given knowledge recognize revelation, submit inwardly, and are guided by God to a straight path, linking receptive reminder to onward direction.
terra: God says He placed no constriction in the religion, defining the revealed course as one fitted against disabling hardship.

luna: The section's passenger is carried on a mount; this ayah says people are carried on livestock and ships, another direct Qur'anic scene of travel by animal. | terra: People are carried “on them and on ships,” placing animal mount and vessel under one travel image.
terra: Noah is told what to say once he and his companions have settled on the ship, another vehicle use of اسْتَوَيْتَ.
terra: The people in the Fire confess that their شِقْوَتُنَا overcame them and that they were astray, joining hardship to loss of route.
terra: God creates creatures that move on bellies, two legs, or four, showing created fitting and guidance through distinct forms of locomotion.
terra: The wrongdoer wishes he had taken a path with the Messenger, expressing missed discipleship as failure to travel behind the right leader.
terra: Those gathered on their faces toward Hell are called worst in place and farther astray from the path, the inverted gait and route of 67:22.
terra: God gives Moses the Book and appoints Aaron with him as a minister, repeating the companion support that answers Moses’ need for strength.
terra: Hearers who fail to understand are likened to livestock and called still farther astray from the path, the failed human opposite of a rightly led animal.

luna: The section's dictionary form هَدْيٌ describes a calm, good manner of walking; this ayah depicts the servants of the Merciful walking gently on earth. | terra: The servants of the Merciful “walk on the earth gently,” the closest Qur’anic staging of the section’s calm, unhurried, good gait.
terra: Whenever a renewed reminder comes from the Merciful, its hearers turn away from it, restaging the deliberate bypass of 87:11.
luna: The section gives a guided route with different responses; this ayah sets up Moses' sea crossing when his companions fear that the pursuing force will overtake them.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance; facing capture at the sea, Moses says his Lord is with him and will guide him, making the guide's role a concrete deliverance. | terra: At the blocked sea during flight, Moses says “my Lord is with me; He will guide me,” so guidance arrives inside an urgent physical journey.
luna: The section develops passage over a difficult route; this ayah has Moses strike the sea and God split it, making a traversable way for the people in 26:61–62.
luna: The section distinguishes travelers by how they take a route; this ayah brings the pursuing force to the crossing too, placing both groups at the same passage before their different ends.
luna: The section connects guidance to the safer course; this ayah says Moses and those with him were saved together, giving the guided group's outcome in the sea crossing.
luna: The section contrasts the wretched traveler's end with the guided way; this ayah says the pursuing group was drowned, completing the opposite outcome to 26:65.
terra: God guides people through the darknesses of land and sea, presenting guidance as practical navigation.
terra: Moses’ sister watches him عَنْ جُنُبٍ, from the side and unnoticed; this preserves the lateral sense behind leading or keeping something alongside.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for showing a road and dictionary form سَوَاءٌ for an even way; traveling toward Midian, Moses asks his Lord to guide him to a sound way. | terra: As Moses physically turns toward Midian, he hopes his Lord will guide him to the level road, making guidance literal route-finding.
terra: The woman approaches Moses “walking with modesty”; this is a particular composed gait, though the ayah does not connect it explicitly to guidance.
terra: Moses asks that Aaron be sent with him رِدْءًا, as supporting reinforcement, closely matching the secondary image of a weak person relying on another.
terra: God promises “We will strengthen your arm through your brother,” answering Moses’ weakness with a companion’s support.
terra: Pharaoh and his chiefs are made leaders who invite to the Fire, a formal reversal of leaders who guide by God’s command.
luna: The section's root ه د ي describes being led along a way; this ayah promises guidance to God's ways for those who strive for Him, linking effort on the path with guidance.
terra: “Do not walk exultantly on earth” supplies the rejected gait whose correction follows in 31:19.

luna: The section's dictionary form هَدْيٌ describes a composed gait; this ayah tells the walker to moderate his pace, giving that secondary walking sense a concrete counterpart. | terra: وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ commands moderation in one’s walk, defining the deliberate pace opposed to panicked flight.
terra: God proportions the human being and gives faculties, another creation use of سوّى that shows fitness before directed human action.
terra: Their sides leave their beds as they call on God in fear and hope; bodily “sides” enact a saving separation directed toward worship.
terra: Leaders are appointed from among the Israelites to guide by God’s command when they show patience, tying guidance to qualified endurance on the course.
terra: People in the Fire confess that they obeyed leaders and great men who misled them from the path, exposing the ruin caused by following false guides.

luna: The section says the fearful remember when reminded; this ayah says only the one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen can be warned, joining fear, following, and reminder in one description. | terra: The warning reaches the one who follows the reminder and fears the Merciful unseen, pairing following with the receptive fearer.
terra: A man comes running from the farthest end of the city and commands “follow the messengers,” joining bodily motion to choosing leaders.
terra: “Follow those who ask no payment and are guided” identifies why the running man’s proposed leaders are fit to follow.
terra: God carries human progeny in the laden ship, another vehicle provided to bear travellers who cannot bear themselves.
terra: God creates counterparts to the ship “which they ride,” explicitly extending the vehicle image beyond the laden vessel.
terra: God’s making livestock for human possession supplies the animals that the next ayah describes as subdued and ridden.

luna: The section's dictionary form يَسْرٌ describes a docile animal that follows readily; this ayah says God subjected livestock to people, some of which they ride. | terra: God subdues livestock for people, “and some of them they ride”; the subjected animal is the section’s readily guided beast made concrete.
terra: The wrongdoers, their kinds, and their objects of worship are gathered into the captive procession that the next ayah guides to Hell’s road.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for the guide who leads ahead; this ayah reverses that role by commanding wrongdoers to be led to the path of Hell. | terra: فَاهْدُوهُمْ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطِ الْجَحِيمِ uses “guide” for prisoners driven to Hell’s road, a deliberate reversal of guidance toward the easy good.
terra: The procession is stopped for questioning after being led toward Hell, distinguishing this ayah’s halt from 37:23’s direction of travel.

luna: The section's dictionary form سَوَاءٌ names a middle or level place; this ayah places a companion in the middle of Hell, turning the middle-place image into the road's wrong end. | terra: The saved speaker looks down and sees his former companion فِي سَوَاءِ الْجَحِيمِ, at the exact “middle of Hell” named by the section.
luna: After the section's 37:55 sight of the companion in Hell, the saved speaker says the other nearly ruined him, making their diverging paths explicit.
luna: The section shows one companion in Hell; this ayah says that without his Lord's favor the speaker too would have been brought there, naming the escape that separates their outcomes.
terra: The rejecters found their fathers astray, identifying the false predecessors whose tracks they hurry along in the next ayah.
terra: They rush headlong upon their fathers’ traces, combining wrong following with a hurried gait opposed to the section’s calm, well-guided walk.
terra: Abraham says “I am going to my Lord; He will guide me,” making his separation and divine guidance a first-person journey.
terra: The well-bred standing steeds foreground a horse’s controlled posture, a plausible Qur’anic counterpart to the easy-guided horse in the dictionary branch.
terra: The scene focuses on the horses’ legs and necks, details that meet the section’s light legs, though the ayah’s disputed action does not itself assert ease.

luna: The section names root ج ن ب for avoidance; this ayah praises those who use that same root to keep away from false gods and turn toward God, clarifying that avoidance can protect rather than reject guidance. | terra: Those who اجْتَنَبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ and turn toward God use avoidance in the saving direction, opposite the person who avoids the reminder.
terra: Those who listen and follow the best of what is said are precisely those God has guided, making ready following the mark of guidance.

luna: The section says the one who fears remembers; this ayah describes God's revealed message moving those who fear Him from trembling to softened hearts and remembrance, giving a specific response to the reminder. | terra: The revelation makes those who fear tremble, then soften to God’s remembrance, and is called God’s guidance; fear, reminder, and guidance converge.
terra: Disbelievers are driven in companies to Hell, a collective journey whose destination matches the wrong road’s fire.
terra: Those who feared God are driven in companies to the Garden, forming the opposite procession on the other destination.
terra: The believing man says “follow me; I will guide you to the path of right conduct,” explicitly assuming the section’s forward guide position.
terra: With shackles and chains around their necks, the condemned are dragged, closely realizing the dictionary’s secondary scene of leading a captive alongside.
terra: The dragged captives are taken through boiling water and into fire, supplying the destination of the movement in 40:71.

luna: The section pictures an animal bearing its rider along an easy route; this ayah says God made livestock for people to ride and use, grounding the image in provision. | terra: God makes livestock so that people may ride some and eat some, an explicit statement of the mount’s provision.

luna: The section develops a mount carrying a passenger; this ayah says people are carried on livestock and ships, completing 40:79's benefits with travel. | terra: Livestock bear travellers just as ships do, expanding the previous ayah’s ride into the shared function of vehicles.
luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance and contrasts the one who follows it with the one who turns aside; this ayah says Thamud preferred blindness to guidance and were seized by punishment.
terra: When favored, the human “turns away and withdraws to his side” in أَعْرَضَ وَنَأَى بِجَانِبِهِ, bodily staging the section’s bypassing refusal.
terra: Revelation is a light by which God guides, and the Prophet guides to a straight path; divine and prophetic leading are distinguished within one route.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for showing the way; this ayah says God made paths through the earth so people may be guided. | terra: God makes the earth a bed and puts roads in it “so that you may be guided,” joining prepared terrain to finding direction.

luna: The section develops the mount that carries its rider; this ayah supplies the ships and livestock intended for riding, which 43:13 shows the rider settling upon. | terra: God creates pairs and provides ships and livestock “which you ride,” supplying the vehicles on whose backs the next ayah’s settling occurs.

luna: The section explicitly gives the dictionary form استوى على ظهر دابته for mounting and settling on an animal's back; this ayah uses that very riding-and-settling scene and adds remembrance of God's gift. | terra: The rider literally settles on the animal’s back in لِتَسْتَوُوا عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِ, the exact riding sense the section uncovers inside سوّى.

luna: The section describes a journey and its destination; this adjacent ayah says the riders return to their Lord, giving the mounted journey an ultimate direction. | terra: After mounting, the riders confess that they are returning to their Lord; the compliant vehicle becomes an image of the journey’s final direction.
terra: Devils bar people from the path while those people think themselves guided, showing subjective ease of following cannot certify the route.
terra: “Seize him and drag him to the middle of Hell” combines a captive being led, physical motion, and سَوَاءِ الْجَحِيمِ, the section’s wrong endpoint.

luna: The section names root ي س ر and then commands a reminder; this ayah says the revelation was made easy on the Prophet's tongue so people may remember. | terra: The revelation is made easy in the Prophet’s tongue “so that they may remember,” explicitly linking ease to the reminder’s reception.
terra: The jinn describe the post-Mosaic book as guiding to truth and to a straight path, recognizing revelation as a road guide.
terra: Those who support God are promised divine support and firm feet, a precise bodily answer to the section’s weak, wavering walker.
terra: God promises the Prophet forgiveness, completed favor, and guidance on a straight path, paralleling the personal promise of being made ready for ease.
terra: الْهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفًا أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ is sacrificial livestock prevented from reaching its destination; this different هدي sense gives a led animal a blocked road.
terra: فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ addresses the same Prophet and joins reminder specifically to the hearer who fears.
terra: وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرَى تَنْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ directly states when reminder benefits, the condition posed in 87:9.

luna: The section links avoiding the reminder with preferring worldly life; this ayah describes someone who turns away from God's remembrance and wants only the life of this world. | terra: The command to turn from one who turned from God’s reminder and wanted only worldly life joins 87’s avoided reminder to its preference for the nearer life.

luna: The section names root ي س ر for ease and then turns to remembrance; this ayah says the Qur'an was made easy for remembrance, joining those two details directly. | terra: “We made the Qur’an easy for remembrance” directly connects the section’s ease with the act some hearers accept and others avoid.

luna: The section joins ease to the call to remember; this ayah repeats that the Qur'an was made easy for remembrance, renewing the same invitation in its own passage. | terra: The repeated promise that the Qur’an was made easy for remembrance shows that this ease remains available after a people’s refusal.

luna: The section joins ease to the call to remember; this ayah repeats the Qur'an's ease for remembrance in a third passage. | terra: A third repetition makes the ease of remembrance the stable road offered across changing warning narratives.

luna: The section joins ease to the call to remember; this ayah repeats the same ease-for-remembrance refrain in a fourth passage. | terra: The fourth repetition confirms that the object made easy is consistently the reminder itself.
terra: Those who fear God and believe His messenger receive a light by which they walk, turning receptive fear and following into enabled movement.
terra: Taking God’s enemies as confidants after truth arrived is again called straying from سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ, a relational act expressed as departure from the road’s middle.
terra: The donkey carrying books pictures a burden-bearing animal whose rider-like load produces no response to revelation, a warning against mere carriage of reminder.

luna: The section joins fear of God with remembrance and ease; here the one who fears God is promised that God will make his affair easy, joining the same stance to ease. | terra: Whoever fears God is granted يُسْرًا in his affair, linking the fearing hearer of 87:10 to the ease promised in 87:8.
terra: سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا presents hardship and ease as successive conditions under God’s making.

luna: The section's dictionary form يَسْرٌ means easy to guide and quick to follow; this ayah calls the earth docile, tells people to walk its slopes, and points from provision to return to God. | terra: God makes the earth ذَلُولًا, docile, and tells people to walk on its shoulders; the road itself becomes the compliant mount imagined by the section.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance and develops walking; this ayah contrasts one who walks fallen on his face with one who walks upright on a straight path. | terra: The contrast between one who crawls face-down and one who “walks evenly on a straight path” makes the traveller’s manner determine how the same journey is made.
luna: The section treats a route as passage across created ground; this ayah says God spread the earth out for people, setting up 71:20's broad roads.

luna: The section's traveler follows a route; this ayah says God made broad roads in the spread earth for people to pass along. | terra: The spread earth lets people travel through its spacious mountain ways, a direct landscape for the section’s light-moving traveller.
terra: The listened-to Qur’an is said to guide to right conduct, so the reminder itself becomes the guide that receptive hearers follow.
terra: The one who turns from his Lord’s reminder is made to enter عَذَابًا صَعَدًا, an arduous rising punishment that joins avoidance to the difficult climb.
terra: The ayah repeatedly permits what is easy of recitation while naming travellers walking through the land, bringing ease, gait, and revelation together.
terra: The trumpet’s day is called a difficult day, setting up the next ayah’s explicit denial that it will be easy for rejecters.
terra: The Day is عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ, explicitly “not easy” for rejecters and thus the eschatological boundary of the promised easy course.
terra: The rejecter of God’s signs is burdened with صَعُودًا, a punishing ascent, giving the section’s mountain ridge its adverse moral route.

luna: The section says the wretched person turns aside from the reminder; this ayah asks why people are turning away from it, naming the same refusal before portraying it as animal flight. | terra: فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ asks why they turn aside from the reminder, the same action the section reads in يَتَجَنَّبُهَا.

luna: The section's dictionary note describes a calm, well-guided walk rather than a defeated rush; this ayah compares the reminder's avoiders to startled wild donkeys, making the opposite gait visible. | terra: Their avoidance of the reminder becomes a herd scene: they are “like startled wild asses,” turning spiritual refusal into animal flight.

luna: The section's calm movement contrasts with a fleeing traveler; this ayah completes 74:50 by saying the donkeys flee from a pursuer, showing avoidance as flight. | terra: The wild asses flee from a lion, completing the preceding ayah’s concrete image of the reminder-avoider rushing away rather than walking calmly.
luna: The section says the fearful remember while the wretched avoid the reminder; this ayah calls the revelation itself a reminder, immediately after the fleeing-animal image in 74:49–51.
luna: The section distinguishes the one who remembers from the one who turns aside; this neighboring ayah says whoever wills may remember, stating the hearer's choice after 74:54.
luna: The section's wider surah says people prefer worldly life; this ayah says people love the immediate life, stating the same orientation before 75:21 names what they leave.
luna: The section contrasts the nearer life with the more lasting Hereafter; this ayah says people leave the Hereafter, completing the preference in 75:20.
terra: فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى repeats the compact sequence “created, then proportioned,” directly echoing 87:2.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for showing a way; this ayah says the path was shown and leaves the traveler grateful or ungrateful, matching the image's guided route and differing responses. | terra: إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ presents one shown road followed in two moral manners, gratitude or ingratitude.
luna: The section joins the reminder to a guided road; this ayah calls the revelation a reminder and says whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.
luna: The section's traveler chooses whether to receive the reminder; this ayah qualifies that human willing remains under God's will.
luna: The section's path ends in ease or the great Fire; this ayah contrasts entry into God's mercy with painful punishment for wrongdoers.
terra: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا joins height and proportioning in one act, matching the section’s observation that settling/rising language sits inside سوّى.
luna: The section contrasts the fearful rememberer with the wretched avoider; this passage begins its paired destinies with the one who transgresses, setting up the worldly preference in 79:38.
luna: The section says people prefer the nearer worldly life; this ayah names that preference as the defining choice of the transgressor before giving his destination in 79:39.
luna: The section's avoider reaches the great Fire; this ayah names Hell as the transgressor's destination, completing the worldly preference described in 79:38.
luna: The section says the one who fears remembers; this ayah describes one who fears standing before his Lord and restrains his soul from desire, the opposite course to 79:38.
luna: The section gives the Fire as the wrong destination; this ayah names the Garden as the destination of the one who feared and restrained desire in 79:40.
terra: The Prophet is a warner specifically for the one who fears the Hour, matching the stance that the fearing person will remember.
luna: The section's 87:9–10 passage commands a reminder that the fearful will remember; this ayah calls the revelation itself a reminder.
luna: The section says the fearful will remember; this neighboring ayah says whoever wills may remember, specifying a hearer's response to the reminder in 80:11.
luna: The section's 87:2–3 sequence moves from creation and measure to guidance; this ayah says the human was created and determined, setting up 80:20's eased path.

luna: The section names root ي س ر for making something easy; this ayah says God made the human way easy, turning the section's passenger-and-route image into a direct statement about human life. | terra: ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ says God then made the human being’s path easy, explicitly joining the road to the section’s causative ease.
luna: The section's image asks how a traveler is guided along a road; this ayah asks where people are going, framing the direction question that verses 27–29 answer.
luna: The section's 87:9–11 passage distinguishes responses to a reminder; this ayah identifies the revelation as a reminder for all worlds, answering the question in 81:26.

luna: The section joins the route to a traveler's response; this ayah says the reminder is for whoever wills to be upright, identifying the direction at stake after 81:27. | terra: The reminder is for whoever wills “to go straight,” presenting reception of revelation as the traveller’s desire for an upright course.

luna: The section's route involves human response under divine guidance; this ayah qualifies the hearer's willing by God's will, completing the choice sequence in 81:26–28. | terra: Human willingness to go straight remains under God’s will, marking the boundary between the rider’s response and the One who makes the course possible.
terra: الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ repeats creation followed by proportioning and balance, the ordinary sense from which the saddle image grows.
terra: The recipient of the record in the right hand receives an easy accounting, extending يسر to the favourable reckoning at the journey’s end.
terra: The invitation to look at how camels were created activates the section’s camel-hump coverings and mount, though riding is not stated here.
terra: The adjacent invitation to look at mountains activates the long mountain ridge placed beside the camel image in the section.
terra: The spread earth supplies the surface across which the preceding camel and mountain images can become a journey, but no guide is named.

luna: The section's 87:9–11 sequence commands remembrance, then distinguishes the fearful rememberer from the one who avoids it; this ayah likewise commands the Prophet to remind. | terra: فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُذَكِّرٌ repeats the command and defines the Prophet’s role as reminder.

luna: The section presents a reminder that benefits some hearers; this neighboring ayah limits the Prophet's role to reminding, clarifying the command in 88:21. | terra: The Prophet is not a controller over the hearers; this bounds his reminding role, while their decision to follow or turn aside remains theirs.
luna: The section's worst person avoids the reminder; this ayah identifies the one who turns away and disbelieves as the exception to the reminder's audience.
luna: The section sends its avoider toward the great Fire; this ayah supplies the punishment for the turner-away named in 88:23.
luna: The section cites the steep pass in 90:11; this earlier ayah says the human was created in hardship, giving the ascent's difficulty a human setting in the same passage.

luna: The section recalls the two heights and the hard ascent; this ayah says God guided the human to two high ways, making the route imagery explicit. | terra: وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ shows two elevated roads and makes guidance itself a view of the two ridges.

luna: The section cites the ascent that the traveler does not attempt; this ayah names the refusal itself, and 90:12–17 explain what that difficult pass entails. | terra: فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ says the traveller did not undertake the steep pass, the direct adverse counterpart to the easier ridge in the dictionary image.

luna: The section cites the unattempted ascent in 90:11; this ayah asks what the steep pass is, introducing the actions that verses 13–17 name. | terra: The question “What will make you know what the steep pass is?” announces that the physical ascent will be interpreted by the following deeds.

luna: The section's image makes a difficult ascent matter; this ayah defines its first step as freeing a neck, giving the pass a concrete ethical cost. | terra: Freeing a bound neck is the first act identified with crossing the steep pass, turning ascent into costly release.

luna: The section names an ascent not attempted; this ayah says its next step is feeding on a day of hunger, specifying another part of the climb. | terra: Feeding during famine is the next content of the difficult ascent, showing what effort on the right road consists of.

luna: The section names a difficult pass; this ayah locates its feeding duty in care for an orphan who is near. | terra: The related orphan identifies one recipient of the feeding that constitutes the pass.

luna: The section names a difficult pass; this ayah extends its food duty to a poor person in misery. | terra: The destitute person in dust identifies the other recipient and keeps the elevated road tied to aiding the lowly.

luna: The section contrasts those who follow guidance with the wretched who turn away; this ayah completes the pass's acts with belief, urging patience and mercy among one another. | terra: Faith and mutual counsel to patience and mercy complete the interpretation of those who successfully take the steep road.

luna: The section makes the route depend on how the traveler proceeds; this ayah calls those who take the pass's way companions of the right. | terra: Those who complete the steep pass are named companions of the right, giving the successfully climbed road its community and destination.

luna: The section gives a wrong destination for the one who refuses; this ayah contrasts the companions of the right with those who reject God's signs. | terra: Those who reject the signs are companions of the left, the opposing company reached by refusing the pass.

luna: The section's wrong road ends in Fire; this ayah closes the opposing road with fire locked around its travelers. | terra: A closed-over fire is the endpoint of the left-hand company, completing the passage’s two-road contrast.

luna: The section names root س و ي in 87:2 for fashioning; this oath describes the soul as fashioned, using the same root in the same sense and making the fashioned creature the subject of the next choice. | terra: The oath by the soul and the One who proportioned it uses سَوَّاهَا immediately before the two moral inclinations are disclosed.

luna: The section's road separates travelers by how they proceed; this ayah says the soul was inspired with its wickedness and piety, specifying the opposed directions behind 91:9–10. | terra: The soul is inspired with both its rebellion and its God-consciousness, supplying the two directions opened by its proportioning.

luna: The section's wider surah says the successful one purifies himself; this ayah likewise calls successful the one who purifies the soul, making the right course's result explicit. | terra: Success belongs to the one who purifies the soul, the right handling of the fitted traveller before the camel story begins.

luna: The section sets the successful purified person against the wretched avoider; this ayah gives the opposite outcome to the soul buried in corruption. | terra: Failure belongs to the one who buries the soul, the opposing direction that leads into the action of أَشْقَاهَا.
terra: Thamud’s collective denial sets the scene for the movement of “its most wretched” and shows that his attack embodies a people’s rejected warning.
terra: إِذِ انْبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا places the same superlative “most wretched” in motion in the story of a she-camel, joining the traveller word to a mishandled animal.
terra: God’s messenger identifies “God’s she-camel and her drink”; this is the divine animal beside the moving أَشْقَاهَا of the preceding ayah.
terra: The people deny the messenger and hamstring the camel, showing where the route of the moving “most wretched” ends.

luna: The section uses 92:7 to show ease for the giver; this ayah identifies the first traveler as one who gives and fears, supplying the conduct that precedes that ease. | terra: Giving and fearing God are the traveller’s dispositions that make the promise of the easy course in 92:7 intelligible.

luna: The section contrasts 92:7 with ease for the giver; this ayah adds that he confirms the good promise, completing the description of the traveler before the outcome. | terra: Affirming the best supplies the immediate response to revelation for which the person is made ready for ease in 92:7.

luna: The section explicitly names root ي س ر for ease and preparation; 92:7 applies the same easing verb to the one who gives, fears, and confirms, making ease the outcome of a chosen course. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَى repeats the section’s promise almost word for word and turns moral disposition into a direction made easy to travel.

luna: The section uses 92:10 for the hard outcome; this ayah identifies the contrasting traveler as miserly and self-sufficient, the conduct that precedes it. | terra: Miserliness and imagined self-sufficiency begin the opposite route whose destination is hardship in 92:10.

luna: The section's hard route in 92:10 follows a refusal; this ayah says the miserly traveler denies the good promise, specifying what 92:10 follows. | terra: Denying the best identifies refusal of the reminder as the rider’s choice before he is made ready for the arduous course.

luna: The section's root ي س ر names ease; here the same verb carries the miserly denier toward hardship, reversing 92:7 and showing that the mount image has two destinations. | terra: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَى uses the same causative “make easy” for the opposite destination, proving that compliance alone does not determine where the mount goes.
terra: The denier’s wealth cannot help “when he falls,” giving the hard route of 92:10 a bodily downward outcome.

luna: The section names root ه د ي for guidance; this oath-surah states that guidance is God's responsibility, placing the route's leading hand with the same speaker who eases it. | terra: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَى makes God the one responsible for showing the route, matching the section’s guide who goes ahead.
luna: The section cites 92:12 on guidance; this next ayah places both the first life and the Hereafter with God, setting the temporal frame for the fire and deliverance in 92:14–21.

luna: After the section's quoted guidance-and-ease pair in 92:12, this ayah warns of a blazing Fire, continuing the path's consequence into the same destination named in Surah 87. | terra: The warning of a blazing fire supplies the destination approached by “the most wretched” in the next ayah.

luna: The section names root ش ق و for the wretched traveler; this continuation says that only the most wretched will enter the Fire, joining the root's hardship sense to the wrong destination. | terra: لَا يَصْلَاهَا إِلَّا الْأَشْقَى joins “the most wretched” directly to entering fire, the same sequence as 87:11-12.

luna: The section says the worst person turns aside from the reminder; this ayah describes the Fire-bound person as one who denies and turns away, specifying that refusal in the same surah. | terra: The most wretched is defined as the one who denied and turned away, exactly explaining the behaviour pictured as passing the reminder by.

luna: The section's root ج ن ب describes keeping the reminder aside; here the most God-fearing is kept away from the Fire, reversing the wretched person's direction in 92:16. | terra: وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا الْأَتْقَى reverses 87:11: the worst person keeps the reminder aside, while the most God-fearing is himself kept aside from the fire.
luna: The section's wider surah calls successful the one who purifies himself; this continuation describes the giver who spends wealth to purify himself, linking the easy course to purification.
luna: The section identifies the giver as one set on the easier course; this ayah clarifies that his giving is not repayment of a favor owed to anyone.
luna: The section frames the course as a journey under divine guidance; this ayah gives the giver's aim as seeking his Lord's face, specifying the journey's orientation.
luna: The section contrasts easy and hard courses; this closing ayah says the giver will be satisfied, completing the easier course's promised end.
terra: God removes the Prophet’s burden, supplying the relief that precedes the repeated promise of ease in the same surah.
terra: The removed load had weighed down the Prophet’s back, a bodily burden that closely complements the supported back and light gait in the section.

luna: The section says hardship and ease can accompany one another; this ayah states that with hardship comes ease, directly articulating that relation. | terra: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا places ease alongside hardship rather than merely after it, clarifying the section’s shared road with differing experience.

luna: The section cites the hardship-and-ease pairing; this adjacent ayah repeats the ease promise, giving the pairing a second, emphatic statement. | terra: The immediate repetition insists again that ease accompanies the difficult stretch.
terra: The panting chargers stage speed and exertion at the opposite pole from the dictionary’s calm, unhurried gait; the link is a deliberate contrast of animal movement.
luna: The section's mount moves easily and its guide walks calmly; this ayah depicts charging animals driving into a gathered host, a forceful mounted movement at the opposite pace.
